name: activerecord
description: Active Record 8.1.4 on the pg 1.7.0 adapter, without a Rails application. Native mode calls ActiveRecord::Base.transaction. Nested cases use transaction(requires_new: true), which Rails documents as a savepoint. Writes use create!. Migrations use ActiveRecord::MigrationContext. Category C and D faults withhold or rewrite statements on the PG::Connection Active Record uses, once, before Active Record sees the error. The command tag is recorded in diagnostics and is not the reported outcome.

modes.description: ActiveRecord::Base.transaction on the connection pool. Pool size is the case pool_max. A nested transaction(requires_new: true) is a savepoint named active_record_N. create! writes the markers. MigrationContext applies and rolls back files under a temporary path. No full Rails application, no database.yml, and no callback is registered on the scored path.

TX-04.independent-inner.reason: Active Record has no propagation mode that commits an inner transaction while an outer transaction stays open on another connection. transaction(requires_new: true) is a SAVEPOINT on the same connection, and a nested transaction without requires_new joins the parent. create! sends the insert when it is called, so there are no deferred outer writes for an inner transaction to commit. The hazard TX-04.3 targets cannot arise. https://api.rubyonrails.org/v8.1.4/classes/ActiveRecord/Transactions/ClassMethods.html

TX-05.explicit-serializable.reason: The documented transaction API is ActiveRecord::Base.transaction with a block. isolation: is an option of that block. TransactionManager, which owns begin_transaction and commit_transaction, is marked :nodoc:. There is no documented call that returns a transaction handle the application later commits. https://api.rubyonrails.org/v8.1.4/classes/ActiveRecord/ConnectionAdapters/DatabaseStatements.html#method-i-transaction
